title: Feature Suppression Side-Channel: Steering Interventions Leak Their Presence Through Residual Activations

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Interesting finding if steering is detectable, but the practical threat model (model or adversary detecting steering) is somewhat speculative for current systems. The causal chain to a concrete safety failure requires one extra step.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Applying steering and measuring residual stream changes is straightforward with existing SAE tools. Training a binary classifier on activations (steering active vs. not) is a standard ML task accessible to CS students.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Very tight deliverable: train a classifier to detect whether steering is active from post-intervention activations and report accuracy. Single clean experiment with a clear binary outcome.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
